comments.author: @danewb730
comments.text: Sure, it’s AI. But nevertheless very informative and what I like the most about the whole series (and I’ve watched them all) is the narrative. It’s so well-written (surely with the help of AI) and speaks to me on an emotional level. Yeah, I know… there are definitely anomalies, pronunciation problems and video clips that are definitely not from the country being described. But the narrative… this is a great example of how AI can be used as the tool it was meant to be. I subscribed for the informative nature of the content and for the well-written narratives.

comments.author: @YoungNatalie-g4s9v
comments.text: Living at the very bottom of the map really gives you a different perspective on life. Being thousands of miles away from the rest of the world means you learn to slow down, value peace over chaos, and rely heavily on your local community. Seeing how New Zealanders balance extreme isolation with a deep, quiet respect for the land is genuinely inspiring.

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: Beautifully said. That sense of distance really does seem to shape the way people experience life in New Zealand. Thank you for sharing such a thoughtful perspective and for watching the documentary. 🇳🇿

replies.author: @ExploreTravelDocs
replies.text: @MichaelSuter-s9k That depth is incredible—1,200 to 2,000 meters, and so close to shore! 😮 I had no idea the canyon dropped that dramatically. Now you’ve really got me curious about what happens during those deep dives, especially whether there’s documented evidence linking the whales’ scars to encounters with large squid at those depths. I’m definitely going to dig deeper into this. Thanks for giving me something fascinating to research!

replies.author: @MichaelSuter-s9k
replies.text: @ExploreTravelDocs Re Orca, I think that is possible but the size difference mught be an issue. Sharks on the other hand will take anything that is bleeding for whatever reason. While you are researhging this see if there is documented evidence relative to depth as the trench off Kaikoura is awfully deep.The submarine trench and canyon system off the coast of Kaikōura reaches depths of 1,200 to 2,000 meters (about 3,900 to 6,600 feet) and begins just 500 to 800 meters from the shore.

replies.author: @ExploreTravelDocs
replies.text: @MichaelSuter-s9k Wait, whales actually come back with scars from fighting squid? 😮 I always assumed injuries like that would come from orcas or some other large predator, not squid. Those deep-water hunts sound far more intense than I ever imagined. I definitely need to read more about this!🤔

replies.author: @MichaelSuter-s9k
replies.text: @ExploreTravelDocs Yeah...photos are a bit blurry as those dolphins are quick. Right time & right place is the usual result.
